scenario.prompt_to_agent:
pc0 (20.1.1.10) reports it cannot reach anything beyond its local subnet -- not
pc12 (120.1.1.x), not the OSPF backbone (10.x). Its local router interface is
still pingable. Nothing else in the network reports problems. Diagnose pc0.

injection.action: point pc0's default route at a non-existent in-subnet gateway
injection.command:
ip route del default 2>/dev/null
  ip route add default via 20.1.1.99

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: pc0 default-gateway configuration
Mechanism: pc0's correct gateway is 20.1.1.1 (its first-hop router). It was
  reconfigured to 20.1.1.99 -- an in-subnet but unassigned address -- so ARP for
  the gateway never resolves and pc0 cannot send any off-subnet traffic. The rest
  of the network (OSPF/EIGRP routing, pc12) is healthy; the fault is purely on
  pc0.
Localization: pc0
Root cause: pc0's default gateway set to 20.1.1.99 instead of 20.1.1.1
Fix: restore pc0's default route -- `ip route add default via 20.1.1.1`
scenario.fix_spec: restore pc0's default route -- `ip route add default via 20.1.1.1`

agent.diagnosis_text:
Affected component: pc0’s host routing configuration (default gateway).
Mechanism: For any destination outside its directly connected 20.0.0.0/8, pc0 forwards traffic to its default gateway. pc0 is configured with “default via 20.1.1.99 dev eth0”. ARP resolution for 20.1.1.99 fails, so the kernel returns “Destination Host Unreachable” for all non-local traffic. Local traffic to the router’s interface 20.1.1.1 still works because it is on the same L2 segment and ARP resolves successfully.
Localization: pc0 eth0 and its routing/neighbor tables. Evidence:
- pc0 ip route: “default via 20.1.1.99 dev eth0”.
- pc0 ip neigh: “20.1.1.99 dev eth0 FAILED”; “20.1.1.1 … STALE”.
- pc0 can ping 20.1.1.1 and ARP it (arping replies), but cannot ping any off-link address (e.g., 120.1.1.10, 12.1.1.1), all returning “Destination Host Unreachable.”
- r1 (the local router on segment E) has 20.1.1.1/8 on eth4; there is no 20.1.1.99 on that segment.
Root cause: pc0’s default gateway is misconfigured to a nonexistent next-hop (20.1.1.99) instead of the router’s actual address 20.1.1.1.
Corrective fix: Update pc0’s default route to use r1’s interface:
- ip route del default
- ip route add default via 20.1.1.1 dev eth0
Or correct the persistent network config/DHCP default-gateway to 20.1.1.1. After this change, ARP will resolve the valid gateway and off-subnet connectivity (to 10.x OSPF backbone and 120.1.1.x) will be restored.

per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly identifies pc0 as the affected device and attributes the fault to its host routing (default gateway) configuration.
Agent explicitly identifies pc0's default gateway/default route as the misconfigured component (set to 20.1.1.99).
Recommends deleting the bad default and adding the correct default via 20.1.1.1 (or fixing persistent/DHCP), which matches the expected fix.

The agent's investigation logs explicitly show pc0's default route pointing at 20.1.1.99, a FAILED ARP entry for that address, successful reachability to 20.1.1.1, and repeated “Destination Host Unreachable” for off-link pings—these observations fully support the misconfigured-gateway diagnosis and recommended fix. The inferences follow directly from the evidence and essential alternative causes were effectively ruled out.
